subject: Annual renewal — true-up reconciliation and upsell coordination
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@skybyte.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: July usage spike + renewal questions

Hi Karthik,

Hope you had a nice weekend. We were reviewing our July dashboard and noticed a ~42% spike in inference hours vs our committed capacity that wasn’t covered by burst credits. Our finance team flagged this ahead of the renewal window (contract up 2026-09-30) and asked for a reconciliation so they can finalize the PO.

Can you share (a) a summary of the true-up amount you’re proposing, (b) whether Redwood can amortize the charge into the renewal or offer a short-term credit to smooth the impact, and (c) if there are any recommended capacity/commit changes to avoid repeat surges? I attached the usage export we pulled (usage-report-July-2026.csv).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is asking for numbers by end of week.

Thanks,
Nina Patel
VP Product
SkyByte, Inc.
Attachment: usage-report-July-2026.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@skybyte.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: July usage spike + renewal questions

Nina — thanks for flagging and for the export. I dug into July and confirmed the spike lines up with an internal batch job that executed multiple night windows and pushed many long-context requests. Short answers inline:

1) Proposed true-up: $23,450 (one-time) — this is the delta between committed capacity and measured usage after applying burst credits.
2) Amortization / credit options: we can either:
   - a) amortize the $23,450 across the upcoming 12-month renewal (adds ~$1,954/mo to committed billing) OR
   - b) issue a one-time credit of $11,725 and roll the remaining $11,725 into the next term as a top-up (hybrid option).
3) Recommended capacity change: bump committed GPU hours by 20% for 12 months, enable a conservative burst cap, and add an autoscale window for late-night batches. That would reduce risk of future true-ups.

I attached our calculation workbook (proposed-amortization-SkyByte.xlsx) and a short breakdown. I’ve cc’d Laura (billing) to confirm invoice options and Monica (CS) to align on the autoscale/playbook.

If that looks ok I can turn this into a formal amendment + invoice today. Would you prefer amortization (option a) or hybrid (option b)?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-amortization-SkyByte.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Nina Patel <nina.patel@skybyte.io>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: July usage spike + renewal questions

Nina / Karthik — looping finance in. We can do either amortize or hybrid; both are straight-forward operationally. A couple notes:

- If you pick amortization (12 months), we'll issue an amendment that increases committed spend and reflects the monthly true-up amortization line. That will simplify PO processing for you (single line item added to the renewal).
- For the hybrid option we need a signed addendum that documents the one-time credit and the portion rolled into the next term. We can cut the credit immediately upon signature.
- Either route requires an updated PO referencing amendment SB-2026-1287-A.

We will produce a formal invoice/credit memo once Nina confirms preference. I recommend hybrid if SkyByte wants immediate relief but still wants to preserve cost predictability.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@skybyte.io>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: July usage spike + renewal questions

Thanks — appreciate the quick analysis. SkyByte would like to take the hybrid approach (option b). Procurement approved the one-time credit to smooth cashflow and prefers the remainder rolled into the renewal as a top-up. Next steps for us: procurement will issue an updated PO referencing amendment SB-2026-1287-A once we receive the addendum and the credit memo.

Two asks from our side: please show the amortized portion as a separate line on the renewal (we need it broken out for internal chargebacks), and can Monica follow up to confirm autoscale guardrails so we can avoid a replay?

If you can send the addendum + credit memo today we’ll have procurement sign by EOD tomorrow.

Nina

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@skybyte.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: SB-2026-1287-A: Addendum, credit memo and final invoice

Hi Nina — attached: final addendum (SB-2026-1287-A), credit memo for $11,725, and the renewed invoice showing the amortized $11,725 as a separate "True-up amortization" line. We also included a short notes section with the autoscale guardrail recommendations Monica provided.

Attachment: SB-2026-1287-A-addendum.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
Attachment: credit-memo-SB1287-11725.pdf (PDF, 7KB)
Attachment: final-invoice-SB1287.pdf (PDF, 68KB)

Once you sign the addendum and send the PO reference we’ll apply the credit immediately and finalize the renewal. Thank you — glad we could get this turned around quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
